export.unity.desc: One PNG per slot and animation. LPC layers are merged into the eight paper-doll slots; layers behind the body go to 2clo with draw order -1. manifest.json carries the page grids, frame timing and draw orders, so the Unity importer needs to know nothing about LPC.

export.flat.desc: All layers composited. LPC standard sheets per animation, one universal sheet, or single frames. For prototypes, Tiled, Godot or engines without a paper doll.

about.title: What PixyGoat is built on
about.lead: PixyGoat is a designer, not an art pack. Everything you stack here was drawn by other people, and it comes with rules. This page has both halves: where the collection comes from, and what you may do with what you export.
about.basis.title: Where the art comes from
about.lpc.title: Liberated Pixel Cup
about.lpc.body: LPC started in 2012 as a competition run by Creative Commons, the Free Software Foundation and Mozilla. It paid artists to draw a base character and a style guide first, and to build on both afterwards, so that art by strangers would fit together. That is the unusual part: one grid, one palette, one set of poses, added to by hundreds of people over more than a decade.
about.collection.title: The spritesheet collection
about.collection.body: The parts in this catalogue come from the asset collection of the Universal LPC Spritesheet Character Generator. Every part sits on the same 64-pixel grid, faces the same four directions and covers the same fifteen animations — which is what makes a body, a shirt and a sword drawn by three different people line up frame for frame.
about.code.title: Why PixyGoat is its own thing
about.code.body: PixyGoat reads that folder and nothing else. It uses the collection's sheet definitions as data — which part exists in which colours and for which bodies — but none of the generator's own code, which is GPL-3.0. That separation keeps the two apart: the licence on this tool is its own business, and neither one has to wait for the other.
about.who.title: Three parties, three sets of rights
about.who.body: Worth keeping apart, because only the middle one is anybody here's to give away.
about.who.artistsBody: They drew the pixels and keep their copyright. Their licence travels with every sprite you export, and there is no way of using the art that skips this.
about.who.toolBody: The code of PixyGoat is under a noncommercial licence: use it, change it, pass it on, as long as you are not making money with the tool itself. Making a game with it is not making money with the tool.
about.who.yoursBody: The selection you assemble — which parts, which colours, which body — is your choice and your file. The pixels inside the exported sheet are still the artists'.
about.legal.title: Rights, credits and licences
about.tool.title: PixyGoat itself
about.tool.body: PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. In one sentence: use it, change it and share it for anything noncommercial, and ask first if you want to earn money with PixyGoat itself. Note what this does not touch: what you build with it is yours, and selling your game is not selling PixyGoat.

about.art.title: The sprites
about.art.body: Each part carries its own licence. Most are CC-BY-SA 3.0 or GPL 3.0, some are OGA-BY or CC0, and several parts offer a choice — then the mildest one you can live with counts. The catalogue shows a seal on every part, and the licence filter greys out whatever terms you do not want.
about.credits.title: Credits ship with the export
about.credits.body: Every export writes CREDITS.txt and CREDITS.csv next to the sheets, one line per part with its author and licence. Ship that file with your game, or copy it into your credits screen. For everything except CC0 this is not optional.
about.strictest.title: The strictest part sets the rules
about.strictest.body: A sheet is one image. If a single layer on it is share-alike or GPL, the whole exported sheet has to be offered on those terms — and under GPL the people you hand it to may pass it on again. If your project cannot live with that, filter those parts out before you build the character, not after.
